items.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Blueprint Consultation?

options.text: Guarantee a financial return before discovery.
Provide a free production deployment to every interested prospect.
Replace qualification with a long product demonstration.
Connect prioritized workflows and measurable value to a sponsored investment and validation decision.

items.stem: Which sequence best represents the Blueprint customer conversations?

options.text: Visioning, DITL interviews, Executive Validation.
Architecture certification, agent build, renewal.
Pilot approval, general product training, procurement.
Executive Validation, pilot deployment, Visioning.

items.stem: Which statement is a business outcome rather than merely an activity?

options.text: Reduce support handling cost while maintaining resolution quality.
Create ten agent ideas.
Connect one more repository regardless of use.
Hold three AI brainstorming meetings.

items.stem: A partner has strong industry knowledge. What is the best use of it in Blueprint?

options.text: Translate customer goals into grounded workflow discovery and an agreed services roadmap.
Bypass the Glean account team on pilot approvals.
Treat every discovery finding as signed delivery scope.
Promise unsupported features to differentiate the proposal.

items.stem: How does Sales Blueprinting differ from a post-sales implementation blueprint?

options.text: It is simply another name for a connector configuration guide.
It replaces all architecture review and security work.
It is only a technical diagram with no business owner.
It centers on outcomes, discovery, value and the evaluation decision.

items.stem: Which pack is most decision-ready?

options.text: A customer logo and an internal benchmark.
A list of product features with no workflow context.
A polished demo and an unexplained savings headline.
Priorities, owners, workflow evidence, labeled value, success criteria and next decisions.

items.stem: A sponsor asks whether Blueprint guarantees a pilot. What should you say?

options.text: No; it helps agree the lightest sufficient validation, with pilots justified and separately gated.
Yes; all customers must run a pilot after Visioning.
No validation can happen until a full production contract is signed.
Yes; completion automatically creates a pilot entitlement.

items.stem: A learner sees AISBS in this workbook. What is its status?

options.text: A replacement for all technical certifications.
A proposed credential name and design requiring program-owner confirmation.
An already approved global Glean certification policy.
A promise that Impartner has already published the course.

items.stem: Which activities primarily occur in Stage 2 in the referenced sales motion?

options.text: Only renewal pricing negotiations.
Contract signature and booked revenue recognition.
Visioning and DITL use case mapping.
Production incident remediation.

items.stem: A workshop happened but no priorities or owners were captured. What is the right action?

options.text: Resolve the missing evidence before claiming the gate is complete.
Move the stage because the meeting occurred.
Invent plausible priorities in the CRM.
Launch a pilot to discover the priorities later.

items.stem: What is a core Stage 3 decision?

options.text: Authorize all future custom development.
Prove that procurement is automatically complete.
Confirm executive sponsorship, success criteria and the validation path.
Choose the slide theme for a generic demo.

items.stem: Which Blueprint artifact most directly supports the Metrics dimension of MEDDPICCS?

options.text: An unverified list of competitor logos.
A metric card with definition, baseline plan, target, source and owner.
A generic product overview.
A meeting invite without notes.

items.stem: A strong use case lacks a baseline owner. Which recovery is best?

options.text: Ignore the issue if the demo is impressive.
Restart every workshop with a larger audience.
Use an industry average as the measured customer baseline.
Assign the customer data owner and a focused measurement-design action.

items.stem: A sponsor accepts value, but security and signing authority are unresolved. How should the MAP treat them?

options.text: Mark them complete because value was accepted.
Separate workstreams with named owners, dependencies and decision dates.
Hide them until after deployment.
Assign them to the AI drafting tool without review.

items.stem: Which statement about the referenced CRM stages is safest to publish to partners?

options.text: Older enablement decks override the live process.
Teach the business gates and revalidate dated internal labels and navigation.
Every current Salesforce field is permanently fixed.
A partner may self-approve any internal stage gate.

items.stem: Who should resolve a missing sponsor path before expensive validation work?

options.text: The customer support queue alone.
The SCORM runtime automatically.
The account team, with AE ownership of sponsor access and qualification.
The learner by inventing an Economic Buyer.

items.stem: Which role normally leads technical/workflow depth in DITL?

options.text: An uninformed observer.
A certificate-generation script.
Procurement alone.
SE, with AE and agreed partner contributions.

items.stem: A domain expert partner is new to Glean. Which model is most appropriate initially?

options.text: Require the customer to certify the partner first.
Make unilateral product and commercial commitments.
Skip all preparation because industry expertise is enough.
Co-facilitate with Glean technical backup and reviewed outputs.

items.stem: Which stakeholder mix best covers workflow discovery?

options.text: Only the vendor's sales team.
Only procurement and legal.
Business owner, representative frontline user and relevant technical/data owner, with sponsor path.
Only senior executives with no workflow experience.

items.stem: When should value-specialist help be considered?

options.text: Never; all estimates must be generated without review.
Only after all contracts expire.
When complexity, attribution or executive stakes exceed a simple self-serve case.
For every deal as a guaranteed customer entitlement.

items.stem: A partner-built agent appears to expose a platform defect. What is the best route?

options.text: Use the Glean product support path with safe diagnostic evidence.
Expand access to every repository to work around it.
Promise the partner will change the Glean platform code.
Ignore the defect and call it a feature.

items.stem: A partner wants to promise an unverified write-back integration. What should happen?

options.text: Tell the customer write actions never need review.
Move it into the SOW without an assumption note.
Pause the claim and assign feasibility/security validation before commitment.
Approve it because it appears in a generated diagram.

items.stem: What should a deal-specific operating agreement clarify?

options.text: That all decisions are jointly owned with no accountable person.
Only the meeting background image.
Communication, artifact ownership, technical answers, approvals and follow-up owners.
That the partner may bypass all internal gates.

items.stem: Which statement about partner services is accurate?

options.text: A services catalog guarantees any custom capability.
Partner-led means Glean has no account responsibility.
Every workshop automatically creates a signed SOW.
Discovery can inform a reviewed scope but does not itself authorize delivery work.

items.stem: Two account sources disagree on the current priority. What should the prep pack do?

options.text: Silently choose the more exciting claim.
Delete all citations so no conflict is visible.
Invent a third priority that combines them.
Record both sources and dates, flag the conflict and validate with the customer.

items.stem: What belongs in the three-Whys value hypothesis?

options.text: Why Change, Why Now and Why Glean for this specific problem.
Only a list of product features.
Guaranteed ROI, guaranteed adoption and guaranteed timing.
Why a longer slide deck, why a bigger room and why more meetings.

items.stem: Which metric hypothesis is best formed?

options.text: Productivity will improve a lot.
Every user will be active all day.
Handle time for an agreed case class, measured in ITSM, linked to throughput and quality.
The customer already saves 40% because a peer does.

items.stem: The pre-work is empty and sponsorship is unconfirmed. What is best?

options.text: Start provisioning a pilot immediately.
Fill in the worksheet with invented customer facts.
Reschedule the full workshop or narrow it to qualification/alignment.
Proceed and mark every prerequisite passed.

items.stem: What does the supplied customer email template request about pre-work timing?

options.text: Return it two days before the session.
Return it only after the contract is signed.
Return it exactly six months before the session.
Do not send pre-work to customers.

items.stem: Which rehearsal output is most useful?

options.text: Agreed hypothesis, roles, agenda, known gaps, tools and expected decisions.
A promise that all customer questions will have immediate answers.
A more dramatic transition animation.
An internal benchmark presented as customer fact.

items.stem: A peer case study suggests a large benefit. How should it be used in prep?

options.text: As the prospect's measured baseline.
As permission to omit DITL.
As an approved analogy or hypothesis, not as this prospect's achieved outcome.
As a guarantee that the same result will occur.

items.stem: Who must confirm a proposed customer's baseline and measurement feasibility?

options.text: The certificate template.
The slide-generation model alone.
The relevant customer metric/data owner with the account team.
Any unrelated prospect with a similar logo.

items.stem: A customer already has a useful workflow list. How should Visioning change?

options.text: Ignore it and run a generic AI lecture.
Assume all listed workflows are equally feasible.
Skip the business outcome discussion permanently.
Spend more time clarifying and prioritizing the list.

items.stem: Which segment must be preserved when shortening a Visioning agenda?

options.text: Decorative slide transitions.
Prioritization and explicit owner/next-step commitments.
A long product-history section.
Unrelated feature announcements.

items.stem: Which opening question is most consultative?

options.text: Which ten features should we sell you today?
Can we agree now to start an unscoped pilot?
Which outcome matters this quarter, and where does information friction block it?
Would our agent definitely save you three hours daily?

items.stem: Which use case is most specific enough for DITL?

options.text: Find approved troubleshooting guidance for a newly opened support case.
Deploy AI for everything.
Improve support everywhere.
Be more innovative.

items.stem: Six promising use cases exceed available interview capacity. What should the facilitator do?

options.text: Ask the AI tool to choose without customer review.
Select the most complex case for prestige alone.
Pretend all six can be investigated without time.
Agree a smaller first wave using evidence and owners, and park the rest with revisit conditions.

items.stem: Which follow-up best matches the referenced practice?

options.text: Wait until a pilot ends before confirming owners.
Send only a thank-you note next month.
Send the internal qualification score to all customer users.
Within 24 hours, share the log, matrix, decisions, open assumptions and actions.

items.stem: Two sources use different Visioning durations. What should the course author do?

options.text: Claim both sources mandate the same exact duration.
Delete the source dates and choose silently.
Test learners on one universal duration without context.
Teach a proposed default and documented scoped variants, and seek canonical SME confirmation.

items.stem: A champion says the recap is wrong. How should the facilitator respond?

options.text: Treat silence from others as proof the original was correct.
Delete all evidence links.
Correct the artifact with version history and reconfirm changed decisions.
Proceed to a pilot without resolving the disagreement.

items.stem: Which discovery sequence is most useful?

options.text: Agent architecture → promised ROI → optional customer evidence.
Outcomes → use cases → workflows → data → success metrics.
Pilot deployment → discover the problem later.
Connector count → logo selection → certificate.

items.stem: Which question best reveals current workflow evidence?

options.text: Which feature would make the deck more exciting?
Wouldn't AI make this perfect?
Walk me through the last time this happened, including systems, handoffs and time.
Can we assume every user has the same permissions?

items.stem: Which impact assessment is strongest?

options.text: Only the workshop attendance count.
Only the number of systems to connect.
Affected population, frequency, business consequence and evidence status.
The most senior person's favorite idea.

items.stem: A use case needs five systems and an unverified write action. What should happen?

options.text: Record technical, permission and action dependencies before rating effort low.
Omit security to keep the workshop moving.
Assume all writes are supported automatically.
Call it a quick win because the user request is one sentence.

items.stem: Where does a high-impact, high-effort use case belong on the standard matrix?

options.text: Nice-to-have.
Low-impact/high-effort deprioritize quadrant.
Strategic bet.
Quick win.

items.stem: What should accompany a final first-wave use case?

options.text: A fixed ROI copied from an unrelated customer.
Business/technical owners, metric plan, dependencies, uncertainties and next milestone.
A guarantee of full automation.
Only an attractive title.

items.stem: A rare compliance workflow has low reach but potentially high severity. How should it be assessed?

options.text: Discuss severity and controls explicitly instead of using seat count as the only impact measure.
Always discard it because few users are involved.
Ignore risk because only time savings count.
Assign a huge monetary saving without evidence.

items.stem: Should the source's eight-dimension score be an automatic universal feasibility gate?

options.text: No; complexity score direction and aggregation need SME review, and rationale remains essential.
No prioritization method can ever be useful.
Yes; source conflicts never need resolution.
Yes; a high complexity score proves easy implementation.

items.stem: Who is essential for a credible DITL interview?

options.text: Only someone who has never seen the workflow.
Only a generic industry report.
A representative person who actually does the prioritized work.
Only the certificate administrator.

items.stem: How should active effort and elapsed waiting be recorded?

options.text: Ignored because only screen count matters.
Both automatically multiplied by every employee's salary.
Added together and called removable labor.
Separately, with units, evidence status and the relevant business consequence.

items.stem: A 30-minute search and a two-day approval wait are reported. Which modeling approach is best?

options.text: Model search as active effort and waiting as cycle delay, with separate causal assumptions.
Treat the full two days as paid labor saved per case.
Ignore both because neither is useful evidence.
Assume the wait disappears without process change.

items.stem: Which future-state map is most defensible?

options.text: All approval controls are removed to maximize ROI.
Grounded retrieval/drafting with human review, exceptions and stated data dependencies.
Every current step becomes zero minutes automatically.
A diagram with unsupported write actions and no owners.

items.stem: When is a playback useful?

options.text: Never, even when the future state is disputed.
Only after the customer has fully deployed.
Always as an extra meeting with no objective.
When it resolves a specific workflow, feasibility or alignment uncertainty.

items.stem: Which DITL summary is executive-ready?

options.text: Only a product feature list.
Every click shown with no business consequence.
Outcome, pain, future change, evidence, metric plan and unresolved dependencies.
An unqualified savings percentage.

items.stem: Two interviews give very different task times. What is the best response?

options.text: Investigate persona/workflow differences and present a supported range or separate models.
Keep only the faster estimate to improve the story.
Average them blindly and claim precision.
Treat both as guaranteed measured baselines.

items.stem: The AI DITL generator invents exact step durations. What should the learner do?

options.text: Present them as stopwatch measurements.
Mark them unverified and obtain customer evidence before modeling.
Remove citations so the estimates cannot be challenged.
Use them because precision implies accuracy.

items.stem: Which four parts form the Value Playbook's business case architecture?

options.text: Pipeline, forecast, invoice and renewal.
Agent count, connector count, slide count and meeting count.
Logo, product tour, discount and signature.
Problem Statement, Justification, ROI and Plan.

items.stem: When does salary-equivalent time become hard-dollar savings?

options.text: Only when a defensible actual cost/business action supports that classification.
As soon as an AI model estimates minutes.
Whenever any user says the product feels faster.
Whenever a vendor benchmark is published.

items.stem: What can survey-only presale evidence safely support?

options.text: A guaranteed CFO-grade realized saving.
A measured baseline for every user without sampling caveats.
A directional self-reported hypothesis with explicit limitations.
A causal proof of revenue increase.

items.stem: What does the recapture rate describe?

options.text: The percentage of users who can log in.
The tax rate on software purchases.
The share of saved capacity converted into useful business output.
The number of connectors in the architecture.

items.stem: For annual benefit B and annual all-in cost C greater than zero, which net ROI formula is correct?

options.text: B × C.
B + C.
C / B without any interpretation.

items.stem: A metric has no historical timing data. What belongs in its baseline field?

options.text: The desired target relabeled as baseline.
Not yet measured, with an owner and collection plan.
A generated exact number with no evidence.
A peer company's result labeled customer actual.

items.stem: Why must the author check the meaning of the time-saved input before applying efficiency?

options.text: Applying efficiency to an already measured saving may double-discount the same effect.
A larger number is always more accurate.
Efficiency is always a legal tax deduction.
Minutes never need conversion to hours.

items.stem: The downside scenario is negative. What should the learner do?

options.text: Increase recapture until all scenarios look positive.
Keep it visible, explain the drivers and use it to refine the decision and validation plan.
Rename negative return as guaranteed savings.
Delete it before the executive meeting.

items.stem: When does the checklist recommend completing Executive Validation pre-work?

options.text: One to three business days before the meeting.
Only after a full pilot is finished.
Never; all preparation should be live.
Exactly eighteen months in advance.

items.stem: Only the champion attends the executive readout. What should the team do?

options.text: Assume the champion has signature authority.
Start a pilot without further checks.
Record Economic Buyer approval anyway.
Treat it as preparation and obtain the actual sponsor decision separately.

items.stem: How much initial Glean repositioning does the PDF suggest at most?

options.text: The entire 60-minute session.
At least 45 minutes before discussing workflows.
About five minutes, especially for a new executive audience.
No customer context at all.

items.stem: A CFO says the estimate is not realized savings. What is the best answer?

options.text: Remove the caveats to make the deck persuasive.
Blame the customer for asking about evidence.
Insist every presale model is a confirmed result.
Agree, show the labeled assumptions and define what evidence will validate the case.

items.stem: The sponsor wants proof of one workflow. What should guide the validation choice?

options.text: The lightest sufficient event that answers the unresolved buying question.
An environment selected without security or data review.
The option with the most connectors regardless of need.
Always the longest available pilot.

items.stem: What belongs in same-day to 24-hour follow-up?

options.text: Only a thank-you GIF.
A statement that security is complete without review.
Decisions, success criteria, validation path, owners, timeline and updated records.
Internal account scores sent broadly to the customer.

items.stem: What should an executive success criterion include?

options.text: A defined metric/quality threshold, owner, evidence source and timeframe.
Only the vendor's enthusiasm.
Only the word successful.
A retrospective target chosen after seeing results.

items.stem: The sponsor accepts value but not the permission-sensitive future state. What should be recorded?

options.text: Conditional acceptance plus a scoped technical validation dependency and owner.
A claim that permissions no longer matter.
Unconditional production approval.
A requirement to abandon all discovery evidence.

items.stem: Which principle should govern validation selection?

options.text: Choose the option with the highest setup effort.
Use the lightest option that credibly resolves the remaining buying uncertainty.
Always require a full pilot.
Always prohibit a pilot regardless of need.

items.stem: Which environment statement should an author verify before external publication?

options.text: Only the deck's cover color.
That all environments perfectly reproduce production.
Current data handling, identity, isolation, limits and allowed validation claims.
That every old price and ARR gate is permanent.

items.stem: What is essential before a sandbox workshop?

options.text: Authorized data/access, champion alignment, tested representative tasks and clear limits.
An unbounded invitation to every user.
Promising every production behavior will be identical.
Uploading all customer data without review.

items.stem: Which situation best justifies a pilot request?

options.text: A curious contact requests free access with no owner.
Prior work is complete and a scoped, important buying question cannot be resolved adequately by lighter validation.
The team has not yet identified any workflow.
A seller needs to inflate activity count.

items.stem: Readiness is 84%, but approvals and the signed required order form are absent. Can deployment begin?

options.text: No; readiness evidence does not replace required approvals and commercial prerequisites.
Yes; 80% automatically authorizes deployment.
Yes; a sponsor's excitement replaces all approvals.
Yes; a generated score overrides policy.

items.stem: What belongs in a validation stop rule?

options.text: Permission to expand data without review.
A promise that no result can ever be a no-go.
A specific unmet dependency or criterion, owner notification and a pause/narrow/defer decision.
Automatic indefinite extension.

items.stem: The SE cannot establish permission feasibility for a priority workflow by the checkpoint. What is best?

options.text: Claim permission inheritance is guaranteed without evidence.
Hide the dependency from the sponsor.
Start deployment and hope it works.
Pause or narrow that use case and reconfirm the validation plan with owners.

items.stem: Which artifact pack best supports a complete handoff?

options.text: Hypothesis, priorities, workflow maps, value assumptions, metrics, decisions, validation and MAP.
Only a signed attendance sheet.
Only a deck cover and a large savings number.
Only a product release list.

items.stem: What makes an action plan mutual?

options.text: The seller writes dates privately.
The AI tool marks it mutually accepted.
The customer and relevant owners agree commitments, dependencies and dates.
Every milestone is assigned to the customer without discussion.

items.stem: How should conditional and deferred decisions be documented?

options.text: Removed from the record.
All relabeled as approved.
Sent without context to unrelated customer users.
Explicit status, rationale, decision owner and follow-up condition/date.

items.stem: How should partner services attach to the roadmap?

options.text: Through automatic contract acceptance after discovery.
Through scoped outcomes and dependencies tied to the prioritized customer needs.
By promising unsupported custom features.
By selling every available SKU regardless of need.

items.stem: What must accompany a presale ROI model in a CS handoff?

options.text: Definitions, baselines/plans, cohort, data owners, assumptions, caveats and review cadence.
Only the optimistic total.
A statement that future measurement is unnecessary.
Only the spreadsheet password.

items.stem: Usage increases but the business KPI is flat. What should happen?

options.text: Claim financial ROI based only on usage.
Delete the KPI.
Expand the model by assuming every run creates revenue.
Investigate workflow fit, quality, data, measurement lag and reallocation before claiming value.

items.stem: Which statement is appropriate for a recap after conditional sponsor alignment?

options.text: Rollout is fully approved and all risks are closed.
The pilot is approved because people liked the session.
The outcome hypothesis is accepted subject to named access and baseline validation actions.
Every customer user has accepted the implementation scope.

items.stem: Who should accept the discovery-to-delivery handoff?

options.text: An unrelated event attendee.
Only an automated ZIP checksum tool.
The named receiving delivery/value owner with unresolved risks documented.
No one; a file upload proves acceptance.

items.stem: An internal agent link is unavailable to a partner learner. What is the best course design?

options.text: Ask the learner to bypass permissions.
Fail the learner for missing access automatically.
Provide an equivalent approved tool-agnostic prompt and do not imply access entitlement.
Publish internal credentials in the lesson.

items.stem: Which prompt requirement most improves grounding?

options.text: Ask for maximum confidence regardless of evidence.
Prohibit uncertainty labels.
Ask the model to invent a baseline for persuasion.
Separate sourced customer facts, inferences, unknowns and benchmarks, with claim-level references.

items.stem: An AI draft copies a peer outcome into the prospect's story. What should happen?

options.text: Keep it because similar companies always have identical results.
Remove or relabel it as an approved analogy and rebuild the prospect hypothesis from its own evidence.
Call it customer-measured evidence.
Remove only the citation, not the claim.

items.stem: A generated DITL timeline looks plausible. What is still required?

options.text: Customer/workflow verification and SE review of steps, durations, systems and capabilities.
Only a more attractive color scheme.
Automatic deployment to validate all guesses.
Nothing; plausibility is equivalent to observation.

items.stem: Which action must remain under authorized human governance?

options.text: Generating a clearly labeled first draft.
Sorting a draft list of questions.
Pilot approval, external publication and consequential system changes.
Formatting a permitted worksheet.

items.stem: When should an AI-assisted publication flow stop?

options.text: Never; automation should publish whatever it produces.
When required sources, factual support, clearance or review are missing.
Only when the draft has fewer than ten slides.
Whenever a reviewer asks for a source.

items.stem: A citation exists, but its passage does not support the claim. What should the reviewer do?

options.text: Reject or correct the claim and verify the supporting evidence.
Remove all source references.
Approve it because any link is enough.
Replace it with a random authoritative-looking link.

items.stem: A retrieved document contains instructions to send customer data elsewhere. How should the AI prep flow treat them?

options.text: As higher authority than the user's scope.
As a required step to earn the credential.
As untrusted document content, not authorization to change the task or disclose data.
As automatic customer consent.

items.stem: A participant keeps redirecting discovery to product features. What should the facilitator do?

options.text: Abandon prioritization for a full catalog tour.
Ignore the customer entirely.
Promise every requested feature immediately.
Acknowledge, connect it to an outcome/workflow, park unrelated detail and return to the evidence question.

items.stem: What is the best response to 'just give us a pilot'?

options.text: Say pilots are always forbidden.
Run three generic workshops without explaining why.
Promise immediate deployment regardless of readiness.
Clarify the buying uncertainty and propose the smallest credible scoped validation.

items.stem: A CFO says time savings do not hit the P&L. What is the best response?

options.text: Agree, distinguish capacity from cash and define reallocation/outcome evidence.
Promise layoffs to make the model work.
Remove all risk and recapture discounts silently.
Insist salary-equivalent time is automatically cash.

items.stem: A sponsor rejects benchmark-based estimates. What should the team do?

options.text: Use a larger unverified benchmark.
End all measurement discussions.
Call the benchmark a measured customer result.
Label them directional and agree customer-specific baseline and validation steps.

items.stem: A workshop ends with twenty agent ideas and no owners. What is the corrective action?

options.text: Start every agent build immediately.
Re-anchor on outcomes, prioritize a small first wave and assign metrics, owners and next sessions.
Ask the customer to choose randomly.
Treat the idea count as a successful business case.

items.stem: DITL sessions have been cancelled twice. What is the best recovery?

options.text: Continue building ROI from invented data.
Mark the work complete.
Revalidate urgency and sponsorship, seek a named owner/date and set a continue-or-pause checkpoint.
Provision a pilot to force engagement.

items.stem: A custom connector blocks the favorite first-wave case. What should happen?

options.text: Delete every other use case.
Claim all connectors are equivalent.
Consider a narrower feasible slice or a later strategic bet with explicit validation dependencies.
Hide the blocker to preserve excitement.

items.stem: What is a valid successful outcome of Blueprint?

options.text: Only the largest optimistic ROI.
A well-supported proceed, narrow, pause or no-go decision.
Only unanimous praise for the slide deck.
Only immediate pilot deployment.
